items.headline: Heat Advisory issued June 1 at 9:33AM AKDT until June 2 at 8:00PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Temperatures 80 to 85 expected in areas away from the inner
channels and outer coast.

* WHERE...City of Hyder, Ketchikan Gateway Borough, and Prince of
Wales Island.

* WHEN...From 10 AM to 8 PM AKDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Individuals not accustomed to these unusually hot
temperatures for this region may experience heat related illnesses.
items.areas: Prince of Wales Island; Ketchikan Gateway Borough; City of Hyder
items.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, and check up on elderly and vulnerable
relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear sunscreen and light loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and

items.headline: Red Flag Warning issued June 1 at 8:55AM AKDT until June 1 at 8:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* Winds...Southeast winds up to 15 mph, gusting as high as 20 to
30 mph.

* Timing...Today, from 1 PM to 8 PM.

* Relative Humidity...As low as 20 to 30 percent.

* Temperatures...As high as 65 degrees Fahrenheit.

* Location...Lower Matanuska Valley, specifically around Palmer,
Butte, and Knik River Valley.

* Impacts...Rapid ignition, growth and spread of fires will be
possible.
items.instruction:
A red flag warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are imminent or occurring now, or will shortly. It is directed
toward fire agencies, and through them to the public.

items.headline: Wind Advisory issued June 1 at 5:35AM AKDT until June 1 at 11:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Northeast winds 30 to 40 mph with gusts up to 60 mph
expected.

* WHERE...Kodiak Island.

* WHEN...Until 11 PM AKDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects and a few
power outages may result. Downed trees are also possible due to
the combination of strong winds and saturated soils from expected
excessive rainfall.

items.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high

Secure outdoor objects.

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued June 1 at 4:22AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
A front approaching the area will bring gusty northeast winds
along the Northern Bristol Bay Coast beginning today. The
strongest winds, up to 45 mph are expected to occur this afternoon
and evening before winds slowly diminish late tonight through
Tuesday morning. A few gusts of 50 to 55 mph can not be ruled out.

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued June 1 at 2:45AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
A strong North Pacific low will bring an prolonged period of
rainfall to the Alaska Peninsula this morning through Wednesday
morning. Rainfall amounts ranging from 1 to 3 inches are expected
with wind gusts ranging from 45 to 55 mph along the the North
Pacific side of the Alaska Peninsula. The heaviest rain is
expected to fall between Monday afternoon and Tuesday afternoon.
However, moderate rain could linger through Wednesday morning
across Chignik.

items.headline: Flood Watch issued May 31 at 11:49AM AKDT until June 3 at 10:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...The following areas, Kodiak Island. This includes the
cities of Kodiak City, Port Lions, Ouzinkie, Old Harbor.

* WHEN...From Monday morning through Wednesday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff from heavy rain may result in flooding

items.areas: Kodiak Island Northeast; Kodiak Island Southwest
items.instruction:

Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.
